concerns.text: The specification assumes that the American Gut Project (AGP) and the Health and Retirement Study (HRS) can be merged by a shared participant identifier (US‑1 acceptance scenario ‘≥ 80 % overlap on participant IDs’). Publicly available AGP and HRS datasets have no common identifier; participants in AGP did not take the HRS cognitive module. This makes the core data‑integration premise infeasible, invalidating any downstream association analysis.

FR‑013 calls for a linear mixed‑effects regression with random intercepts for participant ID, yet each participant appears only once after the merge (cross‑sectional design). Random intercepts are non‑identifiable and add no statistical value, constituting a mis‑specified model. The analysis should use a standard linear regression (or a mixed model only if repeated measures exist).
